cues.en: Ladies and gentlemen, please welcome Judith Bishop. Good afternoon, everybody. Welcome back to the plenary session of the Microsoft Faculty Summit. It's my great pleasure to introduce to you today, Leslie Lamport, who's a principal researcher at our Microsoft Research Silicon Valley Lab. So students and faculty who have taught operating systems courses, as well as anybody who's really used a computer,
cues.zh: 女士们先生们，有请Judith Bishop。大家下午好。欢迎回到微软学者峰会（Microsoft Faculty Summit）的全体会议。今天我非常高兴向大家介绍Leslie Lamport，他是我们微软研究院硅谷实验室的首席研究员。因此，教过操作系统课程的学生和教职员工，以及任何真正使用过计算机的人，

cues.en: will have benefited from Leslie's work on logical clocks, safety and live-less, sequential consistency, and many other parts of operating systems which laid the basis for the safe operation of the computers that we have today as they move from the single desktop to the large number of interconnected devices we have. Leslie, before he joined Microsoft,
cues.zh: 都受益于Leslie在逻辑时钟、安全性与活性、顺序一致性以及操作系统许多其他方面的研究，这些研究为我们今天计算机的安全运行奠定了基础，使其从单一桌面走向了大量互联设备。Leslie在加入微软之前，

cues.en: was a member of certain various prestigious institutions. He was at MRT, at Brandeis University, and at companies such as DEC, Compaq and SRI. In his career, he has also received several honorary doctorates, and he has tried very hard to help scientists see their workers beautiful.
cues.zh: 曾是多个知名机构的成员。他曾在MIT、布兰戴斯大学（Brandeis University）工作，也曾在DEC、Compaq和SRI等公司任职。在他职业生涯中，他还获得过数个荣誉博士学位，并且他一直在极力帮助科学家们认识到他们工作的优美之处。

cues.en: And for that purpose, he also developed something that I think you all know very well, which is lattic. He's now going to go on and try and persuade engineers that there's something else that is beautiful in life, which is mathematics. And that's what he's going to talk to us about today. So, ladies and gentlemen, please put your hands together for this year's AM Turing Award winner, Leslie Lamport. Thank you, Judith. Thinking above the code.
cues.zh: 为此，他还开发了一个我想大家都很熟悉的东西，那就是LaTeX。他现在又开始尝试说服工程师们，生活中还有另一种美丽的东西，那就是数学。这正是他今天要和我们分享的话题。所以，女士们先生们，让我们用热烈的掌声有请今年的图灵奖（AM Turing Award）得主Leslie Lamport。谢谢你，Judith。超越代码的思考。

cues.en: Why do we think? Well, it helps us do most things, like hunting a saber-toothed tiger, or building a house, or writing a program. So when should we think? Well, hunting a saber-toothed tiger, we should think before leaving the cave, when the tiger is charging at you, it's a little late. Building a house before beginning construction.
cues.zh: 我们为什么要思考？嗯，它帮我们做成大部分事，比如猎杀剑齿虎，或者建房子，或编写程序。那么我们什么时候该思考呢？嗯，猎杀剑齿虎时，我们应该在离开山洞前思考，当老虎向你冲来时，就有点晚了。在开工前建房子。

cues.en: You don't want to think about what you're doing when the carpenters are putting the roof on, or at least start thinking about what you're doing. Writing a program, we should be thinking before we start writing any code. How to think? One of my favorite quotes is from the cartoonist Gwindon, who says, writing is nature's way of letting you know how sloppy your thinking is. To think...
cues.zh: 当木匠们在装屋顶时，你可不想再去想自己在做什么，或者至少开始想想你在做什么。写程序，我们应该在开始写任何代码之前就进行思考。如何思考？我最喜欢的一句名言来自漫画家 Gwindon，他说，写作是自然让你知道你的思维有多么混乱的一种方式。去思考……

cues.en: to really think you have to write. If you're thinking without writing, chances are you're fooling yourself. You only are pretending to think. What to write? Well, hunting a saber-toothed tiger. Sorry, writing wasn't invented then, which meant it was a very dangerous activity. Building a house. Well, what you...
cues.zh: 要真正去思考，你必须动笔写。如果你只思考而不动笔，多半是在自欺欺人。你只是在假装思考。写什么呢？嗯，猎杀剑齿虎。抱歉，那时还没发明写作，这意味着那是一项非常危险的活动。建房子。嗯，你……

But blueprints of programs are what we call specifications. Specifications. Well, when I say the word, people tend to panic. This formal stuff that's...
cues.zh: 在开始建房子之前写的东西叫做蓝图。这就叫做画蓝图。编写程序。嗯，你也应该写一份程序的蓝图。但程序的蓝图就是我们所说的规范。规范。嗯，当我提到这个词时，人们往往会恐慌。这些形式化的东西……

cues.en: impossible to read and understand, and you have to learn these funny symbols and all that sort of stuff. Yeah, this is a blueprint, you know, all this complicated stuff going on. But this is also a blueprint. In fact, there's an entire spectrum of blueprints ranging from very detailed, complicated blueprints, which you need if you're building something that's very big and complicated.
cues.zh: 根本无法阅读和理解，你还得去学那些奇怪的符号以及诸如此类的东西。是的，这是一张蓝图，你知道的，里面有很多复杂的东西在运作。但这也是一张蓝图。事实上，蓝图存在于一个完整的谱系中，从非常详细、复杂的蓝图——如果你在建造非常宏大且复杂的东西时就需要这种——

cues.en: At the other end, they're just rough sketch of what you're building is just something really simple that you're going to do in the weekend. And there are these ordinary blueprints for things like a house or the kinds of blueprints that most of us might have seen. And similarly, there's a spectrum of specifications. There are formal specifications.
cues.zh: 在另一端，它们只是你所构建东西的粗略草图，只是你周末要做的非常简单的东西。还有这些普通蓝图，比如房子的蓝图，或者我们大多数人可能见过的那种蓝图。同样，规格也有一个谱系。有形式化规格。

cues.en: of the formal specifications written in a precise formal language. And on the other end, there are just short prose specifications. And in the middle are what I like to call mathematical prose. Most code is really simple. Few sentences of prose will do. Some code is subtle. It requires more thought. And for that,
cues.zh: 由精确的形式化语言编写的形式化规范。而在另一端，则只有简短的散文式规范。中间则是，我喜欢称之为数学散文的东西。绝大多数代码其实都很简单。几句散文描述就足够了。有些代码比较微妙。它需要更多的思考。正因如此，

cues.en: You have to write, it's prose, but you need to be pretty precise. And some code is either very complex or very subtle or critical. And that's especially the case if what you're doing is writing concurrent or distributed system. It is going to be complex and subtle and quite likely critical. And for that,
cues.zh: 你得去写，这虽然是散文，但你需要相当精确。而且有些代码要么非常复杂，要么非常微妙或至关重要。特别是当你正在编写并发或分布式系统时，更是如此。它将会很复杂、很微妙，而且很可能是至关重要的。为此，

cues.en: You should have tools. You should be using tools to check it, to check your blueprints. And if you're going to use tools, it means you need a formal language because tools don't understand prose. So how to write a spec? Well, writing requires thinking. So how to think about programs? We should think about programs like computer scientists, namely like scientists.
cues.zh: 你应该使用工具。你应该使用工具来检查它，检查你的蓝图。如果你打算使用工具，那就意味着你需要一种形式化语言，因为工具读不懂散文。那么如何编写规范呢？写作需要思考。那么该如何思考程序呢？我们应该像计算机科学家那样思考程序，也就是像真正的科学家那样。

cues.en: Scientific thinking is a very successful way of thinking. We know all that it's brought us. And what science does is make mathematical models of reality. For example, the first very successful science was astronomy. The reality, planets have mountains, oceans, tides, and weather, and all sorts of complicating things. But the simple model that's
cues.zh: 科学思维是一种非常成功的思维方式。我们都知道它带来了什么。科学所做的就是为现实建立数学模型。例如，最早非常成功的科学是天文学。现实中，行星有山脉、海洋、潮汐和天气，还有各种复杂的东西。但那个简单的模型

cues.en: got an astronomy pretty far, is to think of a planet, model a planet as a point mass having position and momentum. Computer science. The reality consists of digital systems. Things like a processor chip, a game console, or a computer executing a program. This is what I'll be talking about, computers executing programs. But what I have to say applies to
cues.zh: 让天文学取得了很大进展，就是把行星建模为一个点质量，具有位置和动量。计算机科学。现实由数字系统组成。比如处理器芯片、游戏主机，或执行程序的计算机。这就是我要讨论的，计算机执行程序。但我要说的同样适用于

cues.en: All those other things just as well. So models, there are lots of models that you've probably come across. Touring machines, partially ordered set of events you probably haven't run across that, and lots of models. But two, to my mind, stand out as being the most useful basic models. Functions and sequences of states. So functions, we model a function of
cues.zh: 所有其他东西。那么模型，有很多模型你可能遇到过。图灵机、事件的偏序集你可能没遇到过，还有很多模型。但在我看来，有两个是最有用的基本模型。函数和状态序列。那么函数，我们可以把程序建模为一个

cues.en: we can model the program as a function that maps an input to an output, or multiple inputs to, or possible inputs to possible outputs. In math, the function is very simple. It's a set of ordered pairs. So, for example, the square function on natural numbers, it's this set of ordered pairs. This pair is 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 4, etc. And the element 2, 4
cues.zh: 我们可以把程序建模为一个将输入映射到输出的函数，或多个输入，或可能的输入到可能的输出。在数学中，函数非常简单。它是有序对的集合。例如，自然数上的平方函数，就是这组有序对。这对是0, 0，1, 1，2, 4，等等。而元素2, 4

cues.en: is an element of this set of the fact that the pair 2, 4 is an element of this square function is usually expressed by saying square of 2 equals 4. Now the domain of square, the domain of a function, are all the first elements of those pairs. So for the square function, the domain is the set numbers 0, 1, 2, and 3, etc., also known as
cues.zh: 是这个集合的元素，即对2, 4是平方函数的元素，通常表述为2的平方等于4。现在平方的定义域，函数的定义域，是所有这些对的第一个元素。所以对于平方函数，定义域是数字0, 1, 2, 3等的集合，也称为

cues.en: the natural numbers that I like to write as net. To define a function, what you do is you specify its domain. So to specify square, we say the domain of square is equal to the set of naturals. And for each element x in its domain, we specify what square maps x to, and it maps the value x to x squared. So that defines the square function.
cues.zh: 自然数，我喜欢写成N。要定义一个函数，你需要指定它的定义域。所以要指定平方，我们说平方的定义域等于自然数集。对于定义域中的每个元素x，我们指定平方将x映射到什么，它将值x映射到x的平方。这样就定义了平方函数。

cues.en: Now, functions in math are not the same as functions in programming languages. Math is much simpler. I'm not a programming language expert, so I don't know what those things that programming languages call functions are, but I know what math functions are a lot simpler. Now, the functions model will take you very far, and it's very useful, but it has limitations.
cues.zh: 数学里的函数和编程语言里的函数并不是一回事。数学要简单得多。我不是编程语言专家，所以我搞不懂编程语言里所谓的函数到底是什么，但我知道数学函数要简单得多。函数模型能走很远，也非常有用，但它有局限性。

cues.en: Its main limitation is that it specifies what a program does, but not how it does it. So for example, quick sort and bubble sort compute the same function, but they're very different programs. Also, some programs don't just map inputs to outputs. Some programs run forever. Well, you know, they may stop before the...
cues.zh: 它主要的局限在于，它只说明程序“做什么”，而不说明“怎么做”。比如，快速排序和冒泡排序计算的是同一个函数，但它们是完全不同的程序。而且，有些程序并不只是将输入映射到输出。有些程序会永远运行下去。当然，它们可能会在……

cues.en: The sun explodes, but it's useful to think of them as running forever. For example, operating systems. You can't specify an operating system as a function because it doesn't map inputs to outputs. So for those specifications, you use what I like to call the standard behavioral model in which a program execution is represented by a behavior. A behavior is a sequence of states.
cues.zh: 太阳爆炸之前停止，但把它们看作永远运行是很有用的。比如操作系统。你无法把操作系统定义为一个函数，因为它并不是把输入映射到输出。所以针对这类规约，你会用到我所说的标准行为模型，其中程序的执行由一种“行为”来表示。行为就是一系列状态。

cues.en: And a state is an assignment of values to variables. And a program is modeled by a set of behaviors, behaviors that represent all possible executions of the program. So for example, let's look at Euclid's algorithm. An algorithm is just an abstract program. As you all undoubtedly know, it computes the greatest common divisor of two integers m and n by
cues.zh: 而状态就是变量的赋值。程序则被建模为一组行为，这些行为代表了该程序所有可能的执行。比如，我们来看看欧几里得算法。算法其实就是一种抽象程序。想必大家都知道，它通过以下方式计算两个整数 m 和 n 的最大公约数：

cues.en: initializing x to m and y to n. And then it keeps subtracting the smaller from the larger. And when x and y are equal, then it stops because that x and y equals the GCD of m and n. So for m equals 12 and n equals 18, there's just one possible behavior. It starts with a state in which that assigns 12 to x and 18 to y.
cues.zh: 将 x 初始化为 m，y 初始化为 n。然后不断用较大数减去较小数。当 x 和 y 相等时停止，因为此时的 x 和 y 就等于 m 和 n 的 GCD。所以当 m 等于 12、n 等于 18 时，就只有一种可能的行为。它始于一个将 12 赋给 x、18 赋给 y 的状态。

cues.en: and then subtract the next state is obtained by subtracting the smaller from the larger x from y. So we just state where x equals 12 and y equals 18 minus 12 or 6. And in the next state you subtract the smaller which is y from the larger and you wind up in a state in which x equals 6 and y equals 6 and since x and y are equal you stop. So it's a very simple algorithm. It has just one possible behavior.
cues.zh: 然后，下一个状态是通过用较大的数减去较小的数得到的，也就是从 y 中减去 x。所以我们就得到 x 等于 12、y 等于 18 减去 12 即 6 的状态。再下一个状态，你用较大的数减去较小的数，也就是从较大的数中减去 y，最终得到 x 等于 6、y 等于 6 的状态，因为 x 和 y 相等，所以停止。这是一个非常简单的算法，它只有一种可能的行为。

cues.en: So how do we describe a set of behaviors? Well, first of all, there's a theorem that says any set B of behaviors is the intersection of two sets. A set of behaviors satisfying a safety property and a set of behaviors satisfying a liveness property. So what are safety and liveness? Well, I'm not going to bother going into formal definitions.
cues.zh: 那么我们如何描述一组行为呢？首先，有一个定理说任何行为集合 B 都是两个集合的交集：一个满足安全性性质的行为集合，和一个满足活性性质的行为集合。那么什么是安全性和活性呢？我不打算深入讨论形式化定义。

cues.en: But a safety property is false if and only if it can be violated at some point during the behavior. So partial correctness is an example. Partial correctness is violated if the program stops with the wrong answer. So at some point in the behavior, you can tell that the property was violated, the point at which the program stopped with the incorrect answer.
cues.zh: 但安全性性质是假的，当且仅当它能在行为的某个点上被违反。部分正确性就是一个例子。如果程序以错误的答案停止，部分正确性就被违反了。所以在行为的某个点上，你就能判断该性质被违反了，也就是程序以不正确的结果停止的那个点。

cues.en: The liveness property is one in which you need to see the complete behavior in order to know if it's false or if it's not satisfied by the program. Classic example is termination. You can't tell that the program hasn't terminated by looking at any finite piece of the program. You have to look at the entire behavior to know that it never terminates. So we specify a set of behaviors by specifying a safety property and a liveness property.
cues.zh: 活性性质是这样的：你需要看到完整的行为才能知道它是否为假，或者程序是否不满足它。经典的例子是终止性。你无法通过查看程序的任何有限片段来判断程序是否尚未终止。你必须查看整个行为才能知道它永远不会终止。所以我们通过指定一个安全性性质和一个活性性质来指定一组行为。

cues.en: Now in practice, specifying safety just turns out to be more important because that's where errors are most likely to occur and tend to be more subtle. I mean, liveness is important, just not as important as safety. And so to save time, I'm going to ignore liveness today and just talk about safety. So how to specify a safety property. We specify it with two things.
cues.zh: 不过在实际中，规定安全性最终证明要重要得多，因为错误最容易在那里发生，而且往往更隐蔽。我的意思是，活性也很重要，只是不如安全性那么重要。为了节省时间，我今天就不谈活性了，只讲安全性。那么如何规定安全性属性呢？我们用两样东西来规定。

cues.en: the set of possible initial states, and the next state relation, which describes all possible successor states of any state. So what language should we use to write these things? Well, let's act like scientists. What language do the scientists use? And the language is mathematics. That's the language of science. So the set of initial states that are described by a formula.
cues.zh: 一组可能的初始状态，以及下一个状态关系，它描述了任何状态的所有可能后继状态。那么我们应该用什么语言来编写这些东西呢？好，让我们表现得像科学家一样。科学家使用什么语言？这个语言就是数学。那是科学的语言。所以，初始状态集是用一个公式来描述的。

cues.en: So in Euclid's algorithm, the set of initial states, we initialize, the initial state is one in which x equals m and y equals n. So that is specified, that initial state is specified by this formula. And the only part, this has only one, it's only one possible initial state that satisfies that formula. The next state relation is also described by a formula. And to describe it, I'll use unprimed variables
cues.zh: 所以在欧几里得算法中，初始状态集，我们初始化，初始状态是 x 等于 m 且 y 等于 n 的状态。所以这是被指定的，那个初始状态就是由这个公式指定的。而且唯一的部分，这里只有一个，只有一个满足该公式的可能初始状态。下一个状态关系也由一个公式描述。为了描述它，我将使用无撇号的变量

cues.en: to talk about the current state, or the first state of the pair, and prime variables for talking about the next state. So let's look at the next state relation for Euclid's algorithm. There are two possibilities, either x is greater than y or y is greater than x. So that formula is going to be the disjunction of two formulas. If x is greater than y, then the new value of x, x prime,
cues.zh: 来讨论当前状态，或者这对状态中的第一个状态，并用带撇号的变量来讨论下一个状态。让我们来看看欧几里得算法的下一个状态关系。有两种可能性，要么 x 大于 y，要么 y 大于 x。所以这个公式将是两个公式的析取。如果 x 大于 y，那么 x 的新值，即 x 撇，

cues.en: is equal to what you get by subtracting y from it. So its new value of x prime is equal to the old value of x minus the old value of y. And the new value of x of y is equal to the old value. So that first formula is specified by all pairs of states satisfying x greater than y and in the initial state, in first state, x prime equals x minus y and y prime equals y.
cues.zh: 等于用它减去 y 得到的结果。所以 x 撇的新值等于 x 的旧值减去 y 的旧值。而 y 的新值等于旧值。所以第一个公式是由满足 x 大于 y 的所有状态对指定的，并且在初始状态中，在第一个状态中，x 撇等于 x 减去 y，且 y 撇等于 y。

cues.en: Okay, you understand what I said. And that describes one possibility, or the disjunction of these formulas to the other case, or y is greater than x in the first state, and the value of y in the new state is the value of y in the old state minus the value of x in the old state, etc. So this simple formula describes the next state relation of Euclid's algorithm.
cues.zh: 好吧，你明白我刚才说的意思了。这就描述了一种可能，或者是这些公式在另一种情况下的析取，或者在初始状态下 y 大于 x，并且新状态下的 y 值等于旧状态下的 y 值减去旧状态下的 x 值，等等。所以，这个简单的公式描述了欧几里得算法的下一个状态关系。

cues.en: Let's see how it works, how you get behaviors out of those two formulas. Well, for an example, I'll take m equal to 12 and n equals 18. So to get the initial state, we look at the initial predicates, predicate, and we substitute 12 for m and 18 for n, for n rather. And you see under that substitution, there's only one
cues.zh: 我们来看看它是如何运作的，你是如何从这两个公式中推导出行为的。举个例子，我设 m 等于 12，n 等于 18。因此，为了得到初始状态，我们查看初始谓词，然后将 m 替换为 12，将 n 替换为 18（或者说把 n 替换掉）。你可以看到，在进行这种替换后，只有唯一的一

cues.en: pair of values x and y that satisfy this relation, x equals 12 and y equals 18.
